findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Verify the leaf's deliverable is the contract (alias removal) step of the parent's expand-contract sequence: either add an explicit dependency on the expand story (which made detectors accept both headings simultaneously), or scope this story to include the expand step first — ensuring no in-flight epic ticket is disadvantaged mid-migration.
evidence: Parent: 'Sequenced expand-contract: detectors accept BOTH headings first, the vocabulary and data move under that umbrella, and the alias is removed last. No window in which a ticket is un-reviewable because its heading is in transit.'

Current code: gates.py:136 matches ONLY r'^##\s+Success Criteria' for epics.

findings.finding: The leaf removes ## Success Criteria from the detector files (gates.py, det_floor.py, assemble.py) as its final deliverable — the 'alias removed last' contract step — without implementing or depending on the expand step the parent mandates: 'detectors accept BOTH headings first, the vocabulary and data move under that umbrella, and the alias is removed last.' The current codebase confirms the expand has not been done (det_floor.py:227 and gates.py:136 still match only 'Success Criteria' for epics). After this story ships, any in-progress epic ticket still carrying ## Success Criteria immediately loses clarity-score points and disappears from _SCOPE_HEADINGS scope extraction, creating the 'ticket un-reviewable because its heading is in transit' window the parent explicitly forbids.
findings.location: Scope / Approach sections; parent epic 1386-5e7c-391d-4a74 Scope ('Sequenced expand-contract'); src/rebar/_engine_support/gates.py:136; src/rebar/llm/plan_review/det_floor.py:227; src/rebar/llm/code_review/assemble.py:253
scenarios: An in-flight epic ticket still using ## Success Criteria has this story land before the store migration story runs; it loses _clarity_score points and is excluded from _SCOPE_HEADINGS scope extraction with no bridging window — the scenario the parent's expand-contract sequence was designed to prevent.
